{"parentUuid":"03f8c65a-3fbc-4a0e-95b2-e0973133c335","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01MCEY1FTDqWSj4gMyakYStn","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VwbGLnTpLdyQX4RQ3NCg8v","name":"Read","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\grill-maximization\\SKILL.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6492,"cache_read_input_tokens":201134,"output_tokens":971,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6492,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":971,"cache_read_input_tokens":201134,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6492,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6492},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYor1oEfeKThPDoyNFE9","type":"assistant","uuid":"99585896-1523-446e-93ee-d3f36252d4b4","timestamp":"2026-04-29T21:55:24.031Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"defb4208-8c35-4698-b162-e673f0552e2e","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"99585896-1523-446e-93ee-d3f36252d4b4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1721466f-c90a-44ff-bf4a-71b25e264e04","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01VwbGLnTpLdyQX4RQ3NCg8v","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tname: grill-maximization\n3\tdescription: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n4\tallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Write]\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t# Skill: Grill Maximization\n8\t\n9\t## When to Use\n10\t\n11\t1. `intent-classifier` returns `recommended_action: OPEN_QA_BUNDLE` / `ESCALATE_HUMAN` with `suggested_grill_questions ≥ 5`.\n12\t2. Agent confidence below threshold (CHARTER 0.99 / SCOPE 0.90 / ARCH 0.80).\n13\t3. Multiple downstream decisions converge on a single human-input dependency — bundle them.\n14\t4. Pre-flight before phase boundary or multi-track plan — grill once, deeply.\n15\t\n16\t**Do not** drip 1-2 questions every few minutes. That is the anti-pattern this skill prevents.\n17\t\n18\t## Why\n19\t\n20\tUP-03 §Q5: \"phải luôn cố gắng grill, q&a human trong một lần nhiều nhất có thể, để cố gắng đo được confident score về độ sync giữa human và agent.\"\n21\tD-002 § Q&A C1 = B: target 15-20 / max 25 / split if more.\n22\t\n23\tCompounding effects:\n24\t1. **Sync-rate maximization** — denser bundles produce more Confidence Score (Track 8a) signal per touch.\n25\t2. **Reduced human cognitive load** — 1× full-context bundle beats 5× partial drips.\n26\t3. **Audit trail richness** — bundles preserve the full reasoning chain.\n27\t\n28\t## Doctrine (8 rules)\n29\t\n30\t- **D1 — Bundle Size** — Mini 3-5 / **Standard 15-20** (default) / Max 25 / Split if >25. Detail + examples in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n31\t- **D2 — Cluster Discipline** — group by topic (`A`, `B`, `C`...). 3-7 questions per cluster, 3-5 clusters per standard bundle. No clustering = checklist, not grill.\n32\t- **D3 — Option Defaults** — every Q has 3-4 options + `D: open answer` + safe agent-default (what agent picks if user defers). Lets human skim-answer (\"ok defaults except Q3=B\").\n33\t- **D4 — Question Quality** — each Q must (a) be answerable in ≤1 paragraph, (b) commit to a clear branch per answer, (c) provide options/scope (not bare yes/no), (d) tie to source_evidence/affects_charter/affects_scope/risk. Failing all four = filler; cut.\n34\t- **D5 — Bundle Headline** — 2-3 lines stating: which decision(s) hinge on this; what defaults if ignored; which Confidence Score categories update. Without it, human can't triage which bundle to answer first.\n35\t- **D6 — Grill Up, Don't Grill Down** — when in doubt: ASK if it could change the decision branch, ASK if it reveals user-preference applicable elsewhere; DON'T ASK if purely confirmatory. Better to over-grill 5 min than under-grill 3 sessions.\n36\t- **D7 — Evidence Anchoring** — every cluster references the source evidence (file:line / section). Without evidence, questions feel arbitrary; human distrusts and defers. Format example in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n37\t- **D8 — Confidence Score Hooks** — bundle MUST tag ≥2 of 5 categories (`LANGUAGE / DOMAIN_UBIQUITOUS / DESIGN_THINKING / SCOPE / DECISION_ROUTING`). 1 category alone = not worth human-touch cost; defer or merge.\n38\t\n39\t## Procedure\n40\t\n41\t1. Collect candidate Qs from `intent-classifier.suggested_grill_questions` + your additions.\n42\t2. Cluster (D2). 3-7 / cluster, 3-5 clusters / standard bundle.\n43\t3. Write headline (D5).\n44\t4. For each Q add options + safe-default (D3) + evidence anchor (D7).\n45\t5. Cut filler per D4 quality bar.\n46\t6. Validate count 15-25 (split if >25).\n47\t7. Tag Confidence Score categories (D8); ≥2 required.\n48\t8. Hand off to `qa-escalation` skill, which writes the file.\n49\t\n50\t## Anti-Patterns (don't)\n51\t\n52\t- **Drip mode**: 2-3 Qs every 30 minutes. Catastrophic for human focus + Confidence Score (each mini-touch is too noisy for sync signal).\n53\t- **Filler padding**: scaling to 20 with confirmatory/trivial Qs to hit target. Better 12 sharp than 20 dull.\n54\t- **Yes/no without options**: forces open prose for every reply; slow + inconsistent.\n55\t- **No evidence anchor**: questions feel arbitrary; human defers indefinitely.\n56\t- **Single-cluster sprawl**: 20 Qs in 1 cluster = checklist, not structured grill. Re-cluster.\n57\t- **No `expected_answer_by`**: implies \"whenever\" → never gets answered. Always set deadline.\n58\t\n59\t## Charter-Tier Bundling Caveat (S2 audit finding G1)\n60\t\n61\tWhen a bundle mixes CHARTER-tier (threshold 0.99) and SCOPE-tier (0.90) items: **split**. Charter-tier items must NOT ride a single \"ok defaults\" shortcut alongside scope-tier items. Each charter-tier item gets its own explicit confirmation question (no safe agent-default for `D: open answer`-only fields). Otherwise charter scope is silently absorbed — exactly the orch CF-DOGFOOD-2 pattern UP-02 §1.1 warned about.\n62\t\n63\t## No-Silent-Default Rule (UP-06 amend, 2026-04-29)\n64\t\n65\tIf a question is NEEDED for agent to proceed → MUST be surfaced via `AskUserQuestion` (multi-batch as needed). NEVER use file bundle as \"user might answer here\" with default-after-24h fallback. Mobile-remote scenario means user often cannot edit file at all.\n66\t\n67\tFor questions agent thinks \"would be nice to ask but not blocking now\" → DO NOT include in current bundle. Instead queue in `agent-workspace/memory/observations/queued-grill-<topic>.md` with `fire_when: <track-or-condition>` trigger. The relevant future session re-grills via Ask when condition activates.\n68\t\n69\tResult: every question in a Q&A bundle is one user MUST answer via Ask before agent continues that branch. Bundle question count = AskUserQuestion call count × 4 (rounded up). No \"padding\" with file-only-deferred questions.\n70\t\n71\t## Standard Bundle Skeleton\n72\t\n73\tSee `references/doctrine-detail.md` § Standard Bundle Skeleton + `references/bundle-examples.md` for 3 worked examples (mini, standard, max).\n74\t\n75\t## See Also\n76\t\n77\t- `qa-escalation` — writes the bundle from this skeleton; tracks lifecycle.\n78\t- `user-prompt-intake` — produces input list of `suggested_grill_questions`.\n79\t- `references/doctrine-detail.md` — D1 size table / D7 evidence format / D8 category taxonomy / standard skeleton.\n80\t- `references/bundle-examples.md` — 3 worked examples.\n81\t- D-002 § Track 4 REV-2; UP-03 §Q5.\n82\t"}]},"uuid":"4705786f-04be-4a40-8fef-0807d25db009","timestamp":"2026-04-29T21:55:24.407Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\grill-maximization\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: grill-maximization\ndescription: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Grill Maximization\n\n## When to Use\n\n1. `intent-classifier` returns `recommended_action: OPEN_QA_BUNDLE` / `ESCALATE_HUMAN` with `suggested_grill_questions ≥ 5`.\n2. Agent confidence below threshold (CHARTER 0.99 / SCOPE 0.90 / ARCH 0.80).\n3. Multiple downstream decisions converge on a single human-input dependency — bundle them.\n4. Pre-flight before phase boundary or multi-track plan — grill once, deeply.\n\n**Do not** drip 1-2 questions every few minutes. That is the anti-pattern this skill prevents.\n\n## Why\n\nUP-03 §Q5: \"phải luôn cố gắng grill, q&a human trong một lần nhiều nhất có thể, để cố gắng đo được confident score về độ sync giữa human và agent.\"\nD-002 § Q&A C1 = B: target 15-20 / max 25 / split if more.\n\nCompounding effects:\n1. **Sync-rate maximization** — denser bundles produce more Confidence Score (Track 8a) signal per touch.\n2. **Reduced human cognitive load** — 1× full-context bundle beats 5× partial drips.\n3. **Audit trail richness** — bundles preserve the full reasoning chain.\n\n## Doctrine (8 rules)\n\n- **D1 — Bundle Size** — Mini 3-5 / **Standard 15-20** (default) / Max 25 / Split if >25. Detail + examples in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n- **D2 — Cluster Discipline** — group by topic (`A`, `B`, `C`...). 3-7 questions per cluster, 3-5 clusters per standard bundle. No clustering = checklist, not grill.\n- **D3 — Option Defaults** — every Q has 3-4 options + `D: open answer` + safe agent-default (what agent picks if user defers). Lets human skim-answer (\"ok defaults except Q3=B\").\n- **D4 — Question Quality** — each Q must (a) be answerable in ≤1 paragraph, (b) commit to a clear branch per answer, (c) provide options/scope (not bare yes/no), (d) tie to source_evidence/affects_charter/affects_scope/risk. Failing all four = filler; cut.\n- **D5 — Bundle Headline** — 2-3 lines stating: which decision(s) hinge on this; what defaults if ignored; which Confidence Score categories update. Without it, human can't triage which bundle to answer first.\n- **D6 — Grill Up, Don't Grill Down** — when in doubt: ASK if it could change the decision branch, ASK if it reveals user-preference applicable elsewhere; DON'T ASK if purely confirmatory. Better to over-grill 5 min than under-grill 3 sessions.\n- **D7 — Evidence Anchoring** — every cluster references the source evidence (file:line / section). Without evidence, questions feel arbitrary; human distrusts and defers. Format example in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n- **D8 — Confidence Score Hooks** — bundle MUST tag ≥2 of 5 categories (`LANGUAGE / DOMAIN_UBIQUITOUS / DESIGN_THINKING / SCOPE / DECISION_ROUTING`). 1 category alone = not worth human-touch cost; defer or merge.\n\n## Procedure\n\n1. Collect candidate Qs from `intent-classifier.suggested_grill_questions` + your additions.\n2. Cluster (D2). 3-7 / cluster, 3-5 clusters / standard bundle.\n3. Write headline (D5).\n4. For each Q add options + safe-default (D3) + evidence anchor (D7).\n5. Cut filler per D4 quality bar.\n6. Validate count 15-25 (split if >25).\n7. Tag Confidence Score categories (D8); ≥2 required.\n8. Hand off to `qa-escalation` skill, which writes the file.\n\n## Anti-Patterns (don't)\n\n- **Drip mode**: 2-3 Qs every 30 minutes. Catastrophic for human focus + Confidence Score (each mini-touch is too noisy for sync signal).\n- **Filler padding**: scaling to 20 with confirmatory/trivial Qs to hit target. Better 12 sharp than 20 dull.\n- **Yes/no without options**: forces open prose for every reply; slow + inconsistent.\n- **No evidence anchor**: questions feel arbitrary; human defers indefinitely.\n- **Single-cluster sprawl**: 20 Qs in 1 cluster = checklist, not structured grill. Re-cluster.\n- **No `expected_answer_by`**: implies \"whenever\" → never gets answered. Always set deadline.\n\n## Charter-Tier Bundling Caveat (S2 audit finding G1)\n\nWhen a bundle mixes CHARTER-tier (threshold 0.99) and SCOPE-tier (0.90) items: **split**. Charter-tier items must NOT ride a single \"ok defaults\" shortcut alongside scope-tier items. Each charter-tier item gets its own explicit confirmation question (no safe agent-default for `D: open answer`-only fields). Otherwise charter scope is silently absorbed — exactly the orch CF-DOGFOOD-2 pattern UP-02 §1.1 warned about.\n\n## No-Silent-Default Rule (UP-06 amend, 2026-04-29)\n\nIf a question is NEEDED for agent to proceed → MUST be surfaced via `AskUserQuestion` (multi-batch as needed). NEVER use file bundle as \"user might answer here\" with default-after-24h fallback. Mobile-remote scenario means user often cannot edit file at all.\n\nFor questions agent thinks \"would be nice to ask but not blocking now\" → DO NOT include in current bundle. Instead queue in `agent-workspace/memory/observations/queued-grill-<topic>.md` with `fire_when: <track-or-condition>` trigger. The relevant future session re-grills via Ask when condition activates.\n\nResult: every question in a Q&A bundle is one user MUST answer via Ask before agent continues that branch. Bundle question count = AskUserQuestion call count × 4 (rounded up). No \"padding\" with file-only-deferred questions.\n\n## Standard Bundle Skeleton\n\nSee `references/doctrine-detail.md` § Standard Bundle Skeleton + `references/bundle-examples.md` for 3 worked examples (mini, standard, max).\n\n## See Also\n\n- `qa-escalation` — writes the bundle from this skeleton; tracks lifecycle.\n- `user-prompt-intake` — produces input list of `suggested_grill_questions`.\n- `references/doctrine-detail.md` — D1 size table / D7 evidence format / D8 category taxonomy / standard skeleton.\n- `references/bundle-examples.md` — 3 worked examples.\n- D-002 § Track 4 REV-2; UP-03 §Q5.\n","numLines":82,"startLine":1,"totalLines":82}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"99585896-1523-446e-93ee-d3f36252d4b4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"defb4208-8c35-4698-b162-e673f0552e2e","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"b2481d5f-bcf7-4291-8425-5cad53833da7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_015rWo3mF3BUrxYCp6A4qCW2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BVSagkvXVf42982KJbEdk5","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\grill-maximization\\SKILL.md","old_string":"## Standard Bundle Skeleton\n\nSee `references/doctrine-detail.md` § Standard Bundle Skeleton + `references/bundle-examples.md` for 3 worked examples (mini, standard, max).","new_string":"## Multi-Batch Composition (L-S15-1, S15 PLAN evidence)\n\nWhen a bundle exceeds AskUserQuestion's 4-question hard limit, split into multiple sequential calls within the SAME session turn. Pack densely: prefer **4+3+2** (9 Qs across 3 calls) over 4+4+1 — the 1-Q tail wastes context overhead vs grouping 2 sharper Qs.\n\n**Pattern (S15 PLAN closed 9 queued-grill items via 3 batches)**: Batch 1 (4 governance) + Batch 2 (3 autonomous-protocol inputs) + Batch 3 (2 drift signal mechanics).\n\n**Rule**: minimum 3 Qs per batch when splitting; only the last batch may carry 1-2 if total count forces it. Pack densely: prefer **4+3+2** (9 Qs across 3 calls) over 4+4+1 — the 1-Q tail wastes context overhead vs grouping 2 sharper Qs.\n\n**Pattern (S15 PLAN closed 9 queued-grill items via 3 batches)**: Batch 1 (4 governance) + Batch 2 (3 autonomous-protocol inputs) + Batch 3 (2 drift signal mechanics).\n\n**Rule**: minimum 3 Qs per batch when splitting; only the last batch may carry 1-2 if total count forces it. Total bundle target still D1 standard (15-20).\n\n**Why**: each AskUserQuestion call has setup overhead (system reminder + options serialization + user comprehension cost). Larger batches amortize; below 3, overhead dominates.\n\n## Standard Bundle Skeleton\n\nSee `references/doctrine-detail.md` § Standard Bundle Skeleton + `references/bundle-examples.md` for 3 worked examples (mini, standard, max).","originalFile":"---\nname: grill-maximization\ndescription: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Grill Maximization\n\n## When to Use\n\n1. `intent-classifier` returns `recommended_action: OPEN_QA_BUNDLE` / `ESCALATE_HUMAN` with `suggested_grill_questions ≥ 5`.\n2. Agent confidence below threshold (CHARTER 0.99 / SCOPE 0.90 / ARCH 0.80).\n3. Multiple downstream decisions converge on a single human-input dependency — bundle them.\n4. Pre-flight before phase boundary or multi-track plan — grill once, deeply.\n\n**Do not** drip 1-2 questions every few minutes. That is the anti-pattern this skill prevents.\n\n## Why\n\nUP-03 §Q5: \"phải luôn cố gắng grill, q&a human trong một lần nhiều nhất có thể, để cố gắng đo được confident score về độ sync giữa human và agent.\"\nD-002 § Q&A C1 = B: target 15-20 / max 25 / split if more.\n\nCompounding effects:\n1. **Sync-rate maximization** — denser bundles produce more Confidence Score (Track 8a) signal per touch.\n2. **Reduced human cognitive load** — 1× full-context bundle beats 5× partial drips.\n3. **Audit trail richness** — bundles preserve the full reasoning chain.\n\n## Doctrine (8 rules)\n\n- **D1 — Bundle Size** — Mini 3-5 / **Standard 15-20** (default) / Max 25 / Split if >25. Detail + examples in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n- **D2 — Cluster Discipline** — group by topic (`A`, `B`, `C`...). 3-7 questions per cluster, 3-5 clusters per standard bundle. No clustering = checklist, not grill.\n- **D3 — Option Defaults** — every Q has 3-4 options + `D: open answer` + safe agent-default (what agent picks if user defers). Lets human skim-answer (\"ok defaults except Q3=B\").\n- **D4 — Question Quality** — each Q must (a) be answerable in ≤1 paragraph, (b) commit to a clear branch per answer, (c) provide options/scope (not bare yes/no), (d) tie to source_evidence/affects_charter/affects_scope/risk. Failing all four = filler; cut.\n- **D5 — Bundle Headline** — 2-3 lines stating: which decision(s) hinge on this; what defaults if ignored; which Confidence Score categories update. Without it, human can't triage which bundle to answer first.\n- **D6 — Grill Up, Don't Grill Down** — when in doubt: ASK if it could change the decision branch, ASK if it reveals user-preference applicable elsewhere; DON'T ASK if purely confirmatory. Better to over-grill 5 min than under-grill 3 sessions.\n- **D7 — Evidence Anchoring** — every cluster references the source evidence (file:line / section). Without evidence, questions feel arbitrary; human distrusts and defers. Format example in `references/doctrine-detail.md`.\n- **D8 — Confidence Score Hooks** — bundle MUST tag ≥2 of 5 categories (`LANGUAGE / DOMAIN_UBIQUITOUS / DESIGN_THINKING / SCOPE / DECISION_ROUTING`). 1 category alone = not worth human-touch cost; defer or merge.\n\n## Procedure\n\n1. Collect candidate Qs from `intent-classifier.suggested_grill_questions` + your additions.\n2. Cluster (D2). 3-7 / cluster, 3-5 clusters / standard bundle.\n3. Write headline (D5).\n4. For each Q add options + safe-default (D3) + evidence anchor (D7).\n5. Cut filler per D4 quality bar.\n6. Validate count 15-25 (split if >25).\n7. Tag Confidence Score categories (D8); ≥2 required.\n8. Hand off to `qa-escalation` skill, which writes the file.\n\n## Anti-Patterns (don't)\n\n- **Drip mode**: 2-3 Qs every 30 minutes. Catastrophic for human focus + Confidence Score (each mini-touch is too noisy for sync signal).\n- **Filler padding**: scaling to 20 with confirmatory/trivial Qs to hit target. Better 12 sharp than 20 dull.\n- **Yes/no without options**: forces open prose for every reply; slow + inconsistent.\n- **No evidence anchor**: questions feel arbitrary; human defers indefinitely.\n- **Single-cluster sprawl**: 20 Qs in 1 cluster = checklist, not structured grill. Re-cluster.\n- **No `expected_answer_by`**: implies \"whenever\" → never gets answered. Always set deadline.\n\n## Charter-Tier Bundling Caveat (S2 audit finding G1)\n\nWhen a bundle mixes CHARTER-tier (threshold 0.99) and SCOPE-tier (0.90) items: **split**. Charter-tier items must NOT ride a single \"ok defaults\" shortcut alongside scope-tier items. Each charter-tier item gets its own explicit confirmation question (no safe agent-default for `D: open answer`-only fields). Otherwise charter scope is silently absorbed — exactly the orch CF-DOGFOOD-2 pattern UP-02 §1.1 warned about.\n\n## No-Silent-Default Rule (UP-06 amend, 2026-04-29)\n\nIf a question is NEEDED for agent to proceed → MUST be surfaced via `AskUserQuestion` (multi-batch as needed). NEVER use file bundle as \"user might answer here\" with default-after-24h fallback. Mobile-remote scenario means user often cannot edit file at all.\n\nFor questions agent thinks \"would be nice to ask but not blocking now\" → DO NOT include in current bundle. Instead queue in `agent-workspace/memory/observations/queued-grill-<topic>.md` with `fire_when: <track-or-condition>` trigger. The relevant future session re-grills via Ask when condition activates.\n\nResult: every question in a Q&A bundle is one user MUST answer via Ask before agent continues that branch. Bundle question count = AskUserQuestion call count × 4 (rounded up). No \"padding\" with file-only-deferred questions.\n\n## Standard Bundle Skeleton\n\nSee `references/doctrine-detail.md` § Standard Bundle Skeleton + `references/bundle-examples.md` for 3 worked examples (mini, standard, max).\n\n## See Also\n\n- `qa-escalation` — writes the bundle from this skeleton; tracks lifecycle.\n- `user-prompt-intake` — produces input list of `suggested_grill_questions`.\n- `references/doctrine-detail.md` — D1 size table / D7 evidence format / D8 category taxonomy / standard skeleton.\n- `references/bundle-examples.md` — 3 worked examples.\n- D-002 § Track 4 REV-2; UP-03 §Q5.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":68,"oldLines":6,"newStart":68,"newLines":16,"lines":[" "," Result: every question in a Q&A bundle is one user MUST answer via Ask before agent continues that branch. When a skill's procedure genuinely needs more body than fits, split content to `references/<topic>.md` companion files; SKILL.md keeps the high-density rules + delegates detail.\n\n**Pattern**:\n- SKILL.md body: rules / when-to-use / anti-patterns (≤150 LOC)\n- `references/<topic>.md`: extended templates / examples / sub-rules (no LOC ceiling)\n\n**Examples (Track 6 secondary closure S20)**:\n- `spec-to-wiki/SKILL.md` 227 → 67 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 163 LOC consolidating 5 sub-templates\n- `ubiquitous-language/SKILL.md` 210 → 97 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 120 LOC schema + examples + drift-log\n- `write-a-skill/SKILL.md` 163 → 99 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 88 LOC SKILL skeleton + failure modes\n\n**When NOT to split**: if compression by prose paraphrasing keeps body ≤ ceiling without losing content, prefer compression over split (Phase 0 portability principle: fewer files = less drift surface). Examples shipped self-contained: `crawler-reliability/SKILL.md` 226 → 102, `fastapi-module/SKILL.md` 225 → 122.\n\n**Anti-pattern**: creating `references/` companion file for content that compresses cleanly into prose. Adds file to track without information gain.\n\n## When Porting From Source Repos — Cross-Locale Pattern Extension (L-S18-1, S18 evidence)\n\nWhen porting a regex-based extractor (or any pattern-matcher whose patterns hard-code language-specific terms) from a source repo to stockforge, the regex set is NOT portable — it is locale-sensitive.\n\n**Pattern**: source repo patterns serve source locale; stockforge user is Vietnamese-speaking. Direct port without locale extension yields false-negative on Vietnamese failure phrases.\n\n**Example (Track 8b S18)**: ported `extract_l0.py` from `C:/htdocs/orch-starter`; English-only `\\b(failed|stuck|broken|error)\\b` patterns missed Vietnamese. Added 5 NEW patterns: `bị lỗi` / `mắc kẹt` / `không hoạt động` / `thất bại` / `bug` (loanword). Bilingual extractor without requiring NLP model.\n\n**Discipline**: when porting any locale-sensitive pattern set (regex / keyword list / stop-list / sentiment lexicon), pre-flight checklist MUST include:\n1. List regex/keywords in source\n2. Translate to target locale (Vietnamese for stockforge)\n3. Add target-locale patterns alongside source-locale (bilingual; don't replace)\n4. Test on locale-specific corpus before declaring port complete\n\n**Anti-pattern**: assuming portability based on language semantics (\"regex is language-agnostic\"). The SYNTAX is agnostic; the CONTENT isn't.\n\n## Telemetry Rollup Design — Deterministic Aggregator Before LLM Guardian (L-S19-1, S19 evidence)\n\nFor session-level telemetry rollup (aggregating per-session metrics across many sessions for self-awareness profile), prefer **deterministic Stop-hook aggregator** over **continuous LLM Guardian** as Phase 0 implementation.\n\n**Pattern**:\n- Deterministic aggregator: bash + awk parsing JSONL/TSV at session-end; runs in milliseconds; emits a row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Cost: ~zero LLM tokens; deterministic output; auditable.\n- LLM Guardian: continuous polling + analysis subagent. Cost: ~1-5K tokens per poll; non-deterministic; not auditable without persistence.\n\n**Phase 0 verdict (Track 9 S19)**: deterministic aggregator wins for rollup use case. LLM Guardian reserves itself for **end-of-phase analysis** (when accumulated rollup data needs interpretation, not collection).\n\n**Example**: `scripts/hooks/self-awareness-aggregate.sh` 124 LOC bash+awk only. Reads dispatch.jsonl + component-telemetry.jsonl + .transcript-tokens + .session-hooks.log + sessions/*.md → emits 1 row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Smoke-tested S19; PASS.\n\n**Anti-pattern (already AP-23 catalogued)**: \"Continuous LLM-Guardian\" — running a polling subagent that watches for telemetry events and synthesizes rollup. Wastes tokens; non-deterministic; cost grows with session length. Reserve LLM analysis for batch end-of-phase rollup interpretation, not real-time aggregation.\n\n**Boundary**: aggregator = collection-only (deterministic); LLM analysis = interpretation-only (over deterministic corpus, batch form, when needed).\n\n## End of amendment"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3741,"cache_read_input_tokens":207626,"output_tokens":10005,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3741,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":10005,"cache_read_input_tokens":207626,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3741,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3741},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYosKV8aRXNFkHkawztZ","type":"assistant","uuid":"957aee9a-c644-4e27-b4fc-2c8ebf16c5dd","timestamp":"2026-04-29T21:57:15.040Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"defb4208-8c35-4698-b162-e673f0552e2e","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` rule 1, agents WRITE to `proposals/`; user approve appends this delta to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`.\n\n## Append to `architecture.md` (NEW section, after Forbidden Patterns)\n\n---\n\n## Slash Command vs Skill — Responsibility Split\n\nSlash commands (`.claude/commands/<name>.md`) and skills (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) overlap in form (both are markdown procedure files) but should NOT overlap in responsibility. Per L-S14-2 (skill-vs-command duplication multiplier), duplicating procedure between a `/foo` command and a `foo` skill multiplies maintenance cost AND creates drift between the two when one updates and the other doesn't.\n\n### Responsibility Split\n\n| Concern | Slash Command | Skill |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Trigger** | User explicit invocation: `/<name>` | Auto-discovered by Claude Code via `description:` keyword match |\n| **Audience** | User-facing workflow (command sequence to execute) | Agent-facing procedure (rules to follow when context matches) |\n| **Body shape** | \"When user types `/<name>`, do these N steps\" — imperative checklist | \"When working in context X, follow this discipline\" — declarative rules |\n| **Reusability** | Single workflow tied to a slash invocation | Reusable across many tasks that match the description |\n| **LOC ceiling** | 120 (per drift-signals D1) | 150 (per drift-signals D1) |\n\n### Anti-Pattern: Duplicated Body\n\nIf `/<name>` command and `<name>` skill both exist with overlapping body content, the skill MUST be the source of truth and the command body MUST delegate (e.g., the command body says \"invokes `<name>` skill via Skill tool\" or copy-references the skill's authoritative rules).\n\n**Example (correct)**: `/grill-me` command body is short — describes user-facing trigger; the procedure lives in `grill-maximization` skill, which the command references.\n\n**Example (anti-pattern)**: `/grill-me` command body and `grill-maximization` skill both contain a 80-line \"how to bundle questions\" procedure. When the bundling rule changes (e.g., 4-question max per AskUserQuestion limit), only one gets updated. The drift signal D-DUPL (TBD) flags >50% line overlap between command + skill of similar name.\n\n### Boundary Heuristics\n\n- If the procedure runs once per user invocation → slash command\n- If the procedure runs across many tasks based on context auto-match → skill\n- If both apply: skill carries the body; command is the entry point\n\n## End of amendment\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":46,"oldLines":4,"newStart":46,"newLines":53,"lines":[" - If the procedure runs across many tasks based on context auto-match → skill"," - If both apply: skill carries the body; command is the entry point"," ","+## When SKILL.md Exceeds Ceiling — Companion-via-References (L-S16-1, applied S20)","+","+Per drift-signals D1, SKILL.md ceiling is 150 LOC. Added 5 NEW patterns: `bị lỗi` / `mắc kẹt` / `không hoạt động` / `thất bại` / `bug` (loanword). Bilingual extractor without requiring NLP model.","+","+**Discipline**: when porting any locale-sensitive pattern set (regex / keyword list / stop-list / sentiment lexicon), pre-flight checklist MUST include:","+1. List regex/keywords in source","+2. Translate to target locale (Vietnamese for stockforge)","+3. Add target-locale patterns alongside source-locale (bilingual; don't replace)","+4. Test on locale-specific corpus before declaring port complete","+","+**Anti-pattern**: assuming portability based on language semantics (\"regex is language-agnostic\"). The SYNTAX is agnostic; the CONTENT isn't.","+","+## Telemetry Rollup Design — Deterministic Aggregator Before LLM Guardian (L-S19-1, S19 evidence)","+","+For session-level telemetry rollup (aggregating per-session metrics across many sessions for self-awareness profile), prefer **deterministic Stop-hook aggregator** over **continuous LLM Guardian** as Phase 0 implementation.","+","+**Pattern**:","+- Deterministic aggregator: bash + awk parsing JSONL/TSV at session-end; runs in milliseconds; emits a row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Cost: ~zero LLM tokens; deterministic output; auditable.","+- LLM Guardian: continuous polling + analysis subagent. Cost: ~1-5K tokens per poll; non-deterministic; not auditable without persistence.","+","+**Phase 0 verdict (Track 9 S19)**: deterministic aggregator wins for rollup use case. LLM Guardian reserves itself for **end-of-phase analysis** (when accumulated rollup data needs interpretation, not collection).","+","+**Example**: `scripts/hooks/self-awareness-aggregate.sh` 124 LOC bash+awk only. Reads dispatch.jsonl + component-telemetry.jsonl + .transcript-tokens + .session-hooks.log + sessions/*.md → emits 1 row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Smoke-tested S19; PASS.","+","+**Anti-pattern (already AP-23 catalogued)**: \"Continuous LLM-Guardian\" — running a polling subagent that watches for telemetry events and synthesizes rollup. Wastes tokens; non-deterministic; cost grows with session length. Reserve LLM analysis for batch end-of-phase rollup interpretation, not real-time aggregation.","+","+**Boundary**: aggregator = collection-only (deterministic); LLM analysis = interpretation-only (over deterministic corpus, batch form, when needed).","+"," ## End of amendment"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"957aee9a-c644-4e27-b4fc-2c8ebf16c5dd","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"defb4208-8c35-4698-b162-e673f0552e2e","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Or: defer entire track until tool lands — forfeits time-value of dependent work.\n\n## Rule 3 — Promotion Target Priority (Q-E3 — closed Recommended)","originalFile":"---\nstatus: PROPOSAL\nproposed_at: 2026-04-29\nproposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)\nsource_evidence:\n  - agent-notes.md § L-S11-2 (IMPL-tier-resolution-doctrine)\n  - observations/queued-grill-master.md § Q-B2 (charter/SCOPE-tier hard block; closed S15 Batch 1)\n  - observations/queued-grill-master.md § Q-E2 (promotion frequency; closed S15 Batch 1)\n  - observations/queued-grill-master.md § Q-E3 (promotion target priority; closed S15 Batch 1)\n  - session-plans/pending/003-S15-track-7-constitution-amendments.md § 2 + § 3\n  - decisions/003-up06-track-5.5-sync-layer-selfcap.md § Open Questions (IMPL-tier doctrine)\ntarget_constitution_path: agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md\nmove_when: user explicit approve via reply or `/promote-proposal decision-discipline.md`\n---\n\n# Decision Discipline — DRAFT\n\n> **Status**: PROPOSAL pending user approval. Per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` rule 1, agents WRITE to `proposals/`; user approve moves this to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` and makes it binding.\n\n## Purpose\n\nCodify how decisions get made, how learned rules get promoted, and where the agent has IMPL-tier discretion vs where the agent MUST surface explicit user picks. Resolves the recurring failure mode of (a) silent default-acceptance on charter-tier scope (UP-06 NO Silent File-Defaults) and (b) churn from over-promoting routine rules to charter when a hook would suffice (Q-E3).\n\n## Rule 1 — Tier-vs-Default-Acceptance (Q-B2 — closed Recommended)\n\nA decision's **tier** determines whether default-acceptance is permissible:\n\n| Tier | Default-acceptance allowed? | Mechanism |\n|---|---|---|\n| **CHARTER** | NO — MUST require explicit user letter pick | AskUserQuestion with no auto-fallback; SessionEnd does NOT close the question |\n| **SCOPE** | NO — MUST require explicit user letter pick | AskUserQuestion with no auto-fallback; born-answered Q&A bundle if user offline |\n| **DECISION_ROUTING** | NO (paired with SCOPE per Q-B2 reasoning) | AskUserQuestion explicit pick |\n| **ARCH** | YES with caveat — explicit pick preferred; agent default with transparent flag if user unavailable | Document the default in decision file frontmatter |\n| **IMPL** | YES — agent decides per L-S11-2 doctrine | Routine implementation choice; log in session journal only |\n\n**Anti-pattern**: bundling a CHARTER-tier item with sub-charter-tier items in one Q&A. Per drift signal D3 (charter-mixed-bundle), this masks silent absorption — the high-tier item gets default-accepted along with low-tier items in a single \"OK\" reply.\n\n**Why**: Charter/scope/routing decisions reshape the project's identity, layers, or routing fabric. A wrong default here produces silent drift that compounds across sessions. IMPL choices are reversible by single Edit; charter changes are not.\n\n## Rule 2 — IMPL-Tier-Resolution-Doctrine (L-S11-2)\n\nWhen a SCOPE/CHARTER-level decision is enacted across multiple sessions, the IMPL of any one session has discretion on:\n\n- LOC distribution within budgets specified in the parent decision\n- Bundling vs splitting writes (one Edit vs several)\n- Final text wording within proposal/skill drafts (subject to identity-scope coherence)\n- File-layout decisions surfaced mid-IMPL (path consistency, file split between research vs dogfood, etc.)\n\n**The doctrine**: downstream-alignment cost dominates drafting-text precision. If an IMPL-tier resolution diverges from the parent decision's prose but downstream artifacts (permissions, README, hooks, .gitignore) all align coherently, the **prose is the drafting bug**, not the IMPL. Surface the divergence as a REV-N amendment to the parent decision; do NOT churn downstream.\n\n**Carry-over examples**: D-005 REV-1 ratifies IMPL-S11-2 (path layout) + IMPL-S12-1 (dogfood file split) per this doctrine.\n\n**Anti-pattern**: rewriting the parent decision's prose to match every IMPL nudge. The decision is shipped; the amendment is the audit trail.\n\n## Rule 3 — Promotion Target Priority (Q-E3 — closed Recommended)\n\nWhen an `agent-notes.md` entry becomes promotable (Rule 4 below), promotion target priority is **cheapest first**:\n\n1. **Hook FIRST** (`scripts/hooks/<name>.sh`) — deterministic check, runs without LLM cost\n2. **Skill SECOND** (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) — encodes procedural discipline; LLM-loaded but specific\n3. **Charter LAST** (`agent-workspace/constitution/<name>.md`) — heaviest lift; requires user explicit approve\n\n**Rule of thumb**: if the rule can be expressed as `grep` or `wc` on a known set of files, it's a hook. If it requires judgment or free-form authoring, it's a skill. If it shapes identity, layers, or invariants, it's charter.\n\n**Anti-pattern**: promoting every learned rule to charter. Charter is for invariants; rules and reflexes belong in hooks/skills.\n\n**Examples**:\n- L-S11-1 Phase 0 portability → HOOK (`bash-hook-lint.sh` § L-S11-1 check)\n- L-S14-1 first-draft compression reserve → SKILL (`write-a-skill/SKILL.md` § Best practices)\n- L-S14-4 autonomous_mode + Mode-D coverage → CHARTER (`autonomous-protocol.md` § Mode A/B/C/D)\n\n## Rule 4 — Promotion Frequency (Q-E2 — closed Recommended)\n\nPromotion runs **at phase boundaries only**, not continuously. Manual review by `promote-rule` skill (or fresh-context promotion subagent) at phase boundary; not per-session-end.\n\n**Why phase-boundary**: per-session promotion produces churn (small batches, low signal). Phase-boundary clusters ≥10 entries lets similarity grouping work. Continuous promotion-on-every-note triggers thrash.\n\n**Trigger**: ≥10 new agent-notes since last promotion run, OR phase-boundary checkpoint, whichever first.\n\n## Rule 5 — Provenance Required on Every Decision\n\nEvery entry in `agent-workspace/memory/decisions/` MUST cite at least one upstream source per `proposals/provenance-protocol.md` (or constitution version once promoted). A decision with empty `source_evidence:` is a drift signal (DR-PROV) and will be flagged.\n\n## Anti-Patterns Catalogued\n\n- **Performative SC ticking** (AP-7) — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals.\n- **Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** (AP-5) — re-read all `human-workspace/user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL items.\n- **Bundling CHARTER with sub-charter** (D3 drift signal) — separate bundles required per Rule 1.\n- **Promoting routine rules to charter** — Rule 3 priority forces hook/skill first.\n\n## Acceptance Process\n\nThis proposal moves to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` when:\n1. User reviews and explicitly approves (chat acknowledgment, or `/promote-proposal decision-discipline.md` skill once that exists).\n2. Once promoted, edits to it require the constitution-amendment process (charter-tier change with explicit user prompt + Q&A).\n\nUntil then, this is a **strong recommendation** — agents SHOULD follow it but it is not enforced by deny-list.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":52,"oldLines":6,"newStart":52,"newLines":20,"lines":[" "," **Anti-pattern**: rewriting the parent decision's prose to match every IMPL nudge. Wasted tokens; output already sufficient.\n\n## End of amendment","originalFile":"---\nstatus: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md\nproposed_at: 2026-04-29\nproposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)\nsource_evidence:\n  - agent-notes.md § L-S14-4 (autonomous_mode flag + Mode-D clean-handoff coverage; cliff-vs-injector dispatch)\n  - session-plans/pending/003-S15-track-7-constitution-amendments.md § 2 + § 4.2\n  - decisions/004-up07-context-threshold-opus47.md (Opus 4.7 thresholds 180K/220K/250K)\ntarget_constitution_path: agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md\ntarget_section: NEW § \"Mode A/B/C/D — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\"\nmove_when: user explicit approve; insertion point = after \"## Hard Rules\" section, before \"## When to Escalate\"\n---\n\n# Session Budgets Amendment — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\n\n> **Status**: PROPOSAL pending user approval. Codifies the autonomous-loop handoff dispatch logic shipped in S14 (`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` + `continue-injector.ps1`) as a budget-discipline clause.\n\n## Append to `session-budgets.md` (NEW section)\n\n---\n\n## Mode A/B/C/D — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\n\nPer Opus 4.7 thresholds (D-004): wind-down at 180K / cliff at 220K / hard cap at 250K. The autonomous loop's handoff mechanism depends on which threshold the session crossed.\n\n### Mode A — Stop without budget alert\n\n`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` writes a minimal continue prompt; user's terminal pulls via `continue-injector.ps1` to resume mid-session. Same context window continues.\n\n### Mode B — Cliff reached (≥220K), session must reboot\n\n`budget-watchdog.sh` triggers `session-self-reboot.sh`. Fresh context window starts; new session reads `checkpoints/latest.md` to resume.\n\n**Reason for fresh-context**: past 220K, transformer attention degrades (per session-budgets.md § Quality Cliff). Continuing in the same context produces \"lost in the middle\" effect; agent forgets rules. Fresh context is cheaper than degraded output.\n\n### Mode C — Premature wind-down before cliff\n\n`budget-watchdog.sh` flags mode-C event in JSONL telemetry (`failure_mode: C` per D-003 § 5.5c.5 REV-4); handoff prep proceeds; user resumes via continue-injector.\n\n### Mode D — Clean handoff (S14 addition, L-S14-4)\n\n`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` recognizes intentional close — checkpoint mtime ≤ 60 seconds AND no A/B/C alert fired. Resume reads `checkpoints/latest.md` cleanly. JSONL `failure_mode: D` (NOT a failure; \"D = clean handoff\").\n\n### Dispatch Rule\n\n```\nbudget < 180K + checkpoint fresh                     → Mode D (clean)\nbudget < 180K + no checkpoint                        → Mode A (continue-injector mid-session)\n180K ≤ budget < 220K                                  → Mode C (wind-down; handoff prep)\nbudget ≥ 220K                                        → Mode B (cliff; session-self-reboot fresh ctx)\n```\n\nThe choice between continue-injector (same-context resume) vs session-self-reboot (fresh-context restart) is **deterministic per the budget threshold**, not per agent judgment.\n\n## End of amendment\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":52,"oldLines":4,"newStart":52,"newLines":23,"lines":[" "," The choice between continue-injector (same-context resume) vs session-self-reboot (fresh-context restart) is **deterministic per the budget threshold**, not per agent judgment."," ","+## Verifier Budget by Scope (L-S21-1, S21 verifier evidence)","+","+Sandwich-verifier dispatch budget depends on artifact-set scope:","+","+| Scope | Token cap | Use case |","+|---|---|---|","+| Single-track (1-3 sessions, 1 decision) | 60-80K | Per-track close verification |","+| Multi-track (5-10 sessions, 2-3 decisions) | 100-120K | Mid-phase checkpoint review |","+| Whole-Phase (≥15 sessions, ≥5 decisions, full artifact set) | **150K** | Phase-boundary final verifier |","+","+**Why 150K for whole-Phase**: S21 verifier covering V1-V10 dimensions across 19 sessions + 8 decisions + 7 proposals + 9 constitution files + 31 hooks + 25 skills + 15 commands + 9 agents + Python library consumed 126K tokens / 89 tool uses / 9.7 minutes. {"parentUuid":"43e32e55-e8e1-4758-83d7-850c702eb689","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. 0 if N/A)\nwall_min=0\nif [[ -r \"$DISPATCH\" && -s \"$DISPATCH\" ]]; then\n    first_ts=$(head -1 \"$DISPATCH\" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '\"ts_ms\":[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d':' -f2)\n    last_ts=$(tail -1 \"$DISPATCH\" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '\"ts_ms\":[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d':' -f2)\n    if [[ \"$first_ts\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && \"$last_ts\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then\n        delta_ms=$((last_ts - first_ts))\n        wall_min=$((delta_ms / 60000))\n        [[ $wall_min -lt 0 ]] && wall_min=0\n    fi\nfi\n\n# Header on first run.\nif [[ ! -f \"$ROLLUP\" ]]; then\n    printf 'session_n\\tsession_id\\tts_utc\\ttokens_real\\ttools_used\\tsubagents\\tfailure_codes\\twall_min\\n' > \"$ROLLUP\"\nfi\n\n# Append row.\nprintf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' \\\n    \"$session_n\" \"$session_id\" \"$ts_utc\" \"$tokens_real\" \"$tools_used\" \"$subagents\" \"$failure_codes\" \"$wall_min\" \\\n    >> \"$ROLLUP\"\n\necho \"[$(date -u +%FT%TZ)] self-awareness-aggregate session_n=$session_n tokens_real=$tokens_real tools_used=$tools_used subagents=$subagents failure_codes=$failure_codes wall_min=$wall_min\" >> \"$LOG\"\n\nexit 0","numLines":95,"startLine":30,"totalLines":125}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"95982f88-8065-407b-9c01-8e16f5e3705f","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"defb4208-8c35-4698-b162-e673f0552e2e","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
